sources.content: In the past year, AI browsers have exited in four postures. Arc stopped updating: in May 2025, Josh Miller, founder of The Browser Company, released an open letter announcing the discontinuation of development of this star product, and the whole team turned to the AI browser Dia. Sidekick was absorbed: its team was acquired by Perplexity in the same month, and the product was shut down in August — if you open its official website today, the page will directly jump to comet.perplexity.ai. The Browser Company itself was acquired: in September, Atlassian bought the entire company for 610 million US dollars. The company that makes Jira acquired the company that makes browsers, a deal that was interpreted at the time as a decent exit.

sources.content: Hiring remote workers also increases the hiring pool for many companies, the report said. The survey showed that 83% of employees who report having a disability or chronic illness cite remote work as a key factor in allowing them to work and contribute to their company, while 34% of employees saying being able to care for their family is a top benefit of remote work. But at the $2.75 billion startup GitLab, which helps developers release code faster and more often, remote work is business as usual. That's because GitLab is an all-remote company and doesn't even have any offices, said GitLab co-founder and CEO Sid Sijbrandij. For now, GitLab is still planning on going public this November, although Sijbrandij previously noted that market conditions could force plans those plans to change. Given its shift to a hybrid seat-plus consumption pricing model (combining a fixed, recurring per-user fee with variable charges based on product usage) and the introduction of its Duo Agent Platform, which requires consumption credits, it's not surprising that GitLab issued conservative fiscal 2027 guidance. Meanwhile, with the stock already washed out, it makes sense for management to set a low bar to jump over going forward.

sources.content: Wu & Hogg (Reference Wu and Hogg2006) argued that incoming TS waves interacting with a localised surface feature are scattered due to the rapid spatial distortion of the base flow around the feature. The effect of the surface feature on the instability amplitude is quantified through a so-called transmission coefficient. Xu et al. (Reference Xu, Sherwin, Hall and Wu2016) further investigated the behaviour of incoming TS waves interacting with rapid localised base-flow distortions ( $\lt \mathcal{O}(\lambda \_x)$ , i.e. smaller than the streamwise wavelength of the perturbation). Here, the earlier hypothesised linear dependence of amplification on the surface feature height could not be reconciled by small humps and indentations both destabilising incoming TS waves. Moreover, earlier [...] where the bump height is low, travelling cross-flow instabilities were found to undergo stabilisation. Westerbeek et al. (Reference Westerbeek, Franco Sumariva, Michelis, Hein and Kotsonis2023) performed linear and nonlinear simulations of the interaction between stationary CFI and large aspect-ratio (i.e. width/height ${\gt } 50$ ) smooth humps of varying height and width that featured no recirculation regions. They observed a consistent stabilisation of the fundamental mode of cross-flow instability, defined as the most unstable mode in the baseline case (i.e. no hump present). Higher harmonics were instead consistently destabilised by the hump. Both behaviours were found to be governed by linear production mechanisms. [...] Navier–Stokes (AHLNS) method to investigate the effect of two-dimensional humps that are either smooth or rectangular (i.e. a combination of forward- and backward-facing steps). They reported an increase in the perturbations amplitude downstream of the hump that is proportional to the height of the hump. Moreover, they found that the shape of the hump, i.e. smooth or rectangular, becomes increasingly important when the hump is of greater height.

For complex pipelines with 20 or more jobs, GitLab CI’s DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) execution model delivers 20 to 40 percent faster total pipeline duration by eliminating artificial stage-based sequencing constraints. GitHub Actions’ model requires all jobs in a stage to complete before the next stage begins, creating bottlenecks in complex workflows that GitLab CI avoids. For raw free-tier CI minute economics, GitHub Free’s 2,000 minutes per month significantly exceeds GitLab Free’s 400 minutes per month. At the enterprise scale with self-managed runners, both [...] GitLab CI/CD takes a more powerful but more complex approach. Its pipeline model supports Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) execution, where individual jobs within a pipeline can declare dependencies on other jobs regardless of stage ordering – enabling truly parallel pipelines that are impossible to express in GitHub Actions’ stage-based model. GitLab’s pipeline efficiency features, including parent-child pipeline hierarchies, pipeline-as-code inheritance, and granular rules-based pipeline triggers, give platform engineering teams fine-grained control that larger organizations increasingly demand. sources.content: This year, linear TV viewership continued to diminish, albeit at varying paces. Italy is the country maintaining the highest viewing time, averaging 3h 32mins daily in H1 2026, losing just three minutes compared to the previous year. In Europe, France (2h 41mins) and Spain (2h 36mins) come next, both down by six minutes, closely followed by Germany (down seven minutes to 2h35). The UK saw the biggest drop, down nine minutes to 2h, while the Netherlands has the lowest viewing time at 1h57, despite dropping by only three minutes. By comparison, the loss last year for all these countries was 10 minutes or more. SVoD and AVoD streaming platforms’ share of video consumption remained stable in France at 11%, and increased slightly (+1 percentage point) to 18% in the UK. [...] Glance 2 Glance 2 Frédéric Vaulpré Video sharing platforms, however, continue to grow, according to Frédéric Vaulpré, senior vice president at The Glance, who his findings during a presentation at Mipcom this week. Linear broadcasters have had on average 12% fewer new series so far across the 48 territories surveyed by Glance, he said. There was also a 12% drop at Netflix, 41% at Disney+, and 45% at Apple TV+, Vaulpré added, although Prime Video’s launches were largely stable. In some areas, streamer catalogues continue to grow significantly, but this is thanks to the addition of third-party content. In France, Netflix’s catalogue volume increased by 61% to reach 74,000 hours when including TF1+, while Prime Video’s catalogue grew by 49% following its deals with France.tv and M6+.
